# Phase Three — Thirty Additional Improvements

The Awtsmoos renews the plan before the plan renews the page;
Awtsmoos.com gains speed when restraint and ambition become partners on one stage.

1. Scope selectors by an actual route attribute already present in production HTML.
2. Never introduce a wrapper solely to satisfy CSS scope when the body route marker already exists.
3. Preserve existing design tokens; do not fork colors or spacing into Apps-only duplicates without need.
4. Keep the Apps manifest import-only so stylesheet responsibilities remain visible.
5. Route-scope media-query selectors too; media queries do not excuse global ownership.
6. Put hover motion behind hover-capable pointer media conditions.
7. Preserve active feedback for touch even when hover is unavailable.
8. Preserve focus-visible outlines independently of hover animation.
9. Ensure reduced-motion rules remain route-scoped and state-equivalent.
10. Keep sticky filter z-index small and local; do not escalate it to solve unknown overlay issues.
11. Verify sticky filter top offsets against the actual shell rather than inventing a new fixed header height.
12. Do not add backdrop-filter animation; keep mobile GPU work bounded.
13. Avoid `100vw`; use available containing block width and `min-width: 0` where spill is possible.
14. Ensure grid tracks use `minmax(0, ...)` whenever content can contain long route/title text.
15. Preserve `content-visibility` optimization on cards while checking keyboard focus behavior.
16. Keep catalog data immutable and separate from presentation.
17. Do not put AI-specific metadata into every visible app card; use progressive disclosure or docs links.
18. Do not force Kabbalistic terms into public labels or API verbs; internal poetry must not become usability tax.
19. Make every new JS lifecycle abortable if it registers route-owned listeners.
20. Keep DOM construction through `textContent`/native elements rather than unsafe HTML strings.
21. Treat any global-style scanner finding as a hypothesis until its stylesheet consumer is known.
22. Exclude vendor/generated/minified styles from rewrite automation; report them separately.
23. Rank global-style findings by public reach and collision likelihood, not raw count.
24. Rank overflow findings by narrowest supported mobile viewport first.
25. Record z-index with its local stacking context; a number alone does not prove a defect.
26. Separate hidden advanced UI from essential navigation so disclosure cannot conceal the primary task.
27. Prefer native `<details>` for simple disclosure; use custom drawers only when lifecycle/focus semantics demand them.
28. Verify docs links against actual files/routes before surfacing them in catalog UI.
29. Re-read recent Animator files before any crosslink because that branch is actively landing its contract.
30. Make the completion statement proportional to evidence: say which route families were changed and which were scanned, not “all pages fixed” without runtime proof.
31. Add a regression proof that all Apps-local selectors include the route scope after rewrite.
32. Test source line counts after rewrites so modularity remains measurable.
33. Keep CSS comment poetry and architectural explanation; split files rather than deleting documentation.
34. Use one source rewrite pass, then test; only perform a second source pass for observed deltas.
35. Preserve existing catalog links exactly unless route validation proves one is dead.
36. If global docs already expose a machine manifest, link to it rather than inventing another endpoint.
37. If no global manifest exists, prefer a small manifest that references specialist manifests rather than one giant duplicated schema.
38. Treat browser runtime screenshots as proof of geometry, not proof of keyboard/API behavior.
39. Test keyboard and API behavior separately from visual verification.
40. Leave durable remaining-work nodes for high-risk surfaces not yet runtime-tested.

## Final refinement

The first concrete production change will be a full-file route-scope rewrite of the Apps stylesheet family after every member is read. It will preserve current UX strengths while eliminating selector leakage and modality errors. The next evidence-producing change will be a reusable static risk scan only if no equivalent tool already exists. Animator remains a verification/crosslink target until its active implementation finishes.
